result.summary: 本文提出了“精度感知”的缩放定律，将训练精度和推理精度纳入语言模型损失预测 [abstract]。作者提出低精度训练会降低模型的有效参数量，并据此预测低精度训练和后训练量化带来的额外损失 [abstract]。对于推理，后训练量化带来的退化随训练数据增加而增大，最终使额外的预训练数据变得有害 [abstract]。作者在超过 465 次预训练运行上拟合，并在高达 1.7B 参数、26B token 的模型上验证了预测 [abstract]。

research_question.text: 论文要解决的问题是：精度、参数量和数据之间存在怎样的权衡，以及这些权衡在预训练和推理时有何不同 [S1.p1]。原文指出，精度是同时影响成本和性能的第三个重要因素，而当前的缩放定律并未考虑这一点 [S1.p1]。

evidence.quote: What are the tradeoffs between precision, parameters, and data? How do they compare for pretraining and inference?
However, the precision in which models are trained and served is an important third factor that contributes to both cost and performance.

method.text: 论文提出用“有效参数量” N_eff 来统一建模精度与参数量的互换关系，并假设量化实现细节仅通过影响 N_eff 来影响损失缩放 [S1.p2]。对于训练，作者将 Chinchilla 缩放形式中的 N 替换为 N_eff(N, P_w)=N(1-e^{-P_w/γ_w}) [S4.SS1.p2][S4.SS1.p3]。对于权重、激活和 KV 缓存的联合量化，作者提出独立乘性的 N_eff 形式 [S4.SS2.p4][S4.SS2.p5]。最终将训练和推理的缩放定律统一为包含后训练量化退化项 δ_PTQ 的单一函数形式 [S5.p8]。

evidence.quote: This functional form that posits bit precision and parameter count interchangeably contribute to a model’s “effective parameter count,” $N_{\text{eff}}$
we find the best fit for the tradeoff between weight precision and parameters is $N_{\text{eff}}(N,P_{\text{w}})=N(1-e^{-P_{\text{w}}/\gamma_{\text{w}}})$
$L(N,D)=A[N(1-e^{-P_{\text{w}}/\gamma_{\text{w}}})]^{-\alpha}+BD^{-\beta}+E$
$N_{\text{eff}}(P)=N(1-e^{-P_{\text{w}}/\gamma_{\text{w}}})(1-e^{-P_{\text{a}}/\gamma_{\text{a}}})(1-e^{-P_{\text{kv}}/\gamma_{\text{kv}}})$
The effects of quantizing the weights, activations, and KV cache during training are well modeled as independent and multiplicative

the predicted loss for a language model with $N$ parameters, trained on $D$ tokens, with training precision $P_{\text{w}},P_{\text{a}},P_{\text{kv}}$ to end-time weight-precision $P_{\text{post}}$, can be predicted as $L(N,D,P_{\text{w}},P_{\text{a}},P_{\text{kv}},P_{\text{post}})=AN_{\text{eff}}^{-\alpha}+BD^{-\beta}+E+\delta_{\text{PTQ}}$

experiments.text: 作者在 Dolma V1.7 数据集上训练和评估了一系列 OLMo 风格的模型，使用标准 Transformer++ 实现 [S2.SS3.p1]。实验扫描了 N∈[30,60,110,220] 百万非嵌入参数和 D∈[1.5,3,6,13,26] 十亿 token，每个 (N,D) 组合运行超过 20 次，并扫描 8 个精度值 [S2.SS3.p1]。训练精度扫描覆盖 P_w,P_a,P_kv∈[3,12] 以及 BF16 基线 [S4.p1]。作者在超过 465 次预训练运行上拟合，并在高达 1.7B 参数、26B token 的模型上验证预测 [abstract]。

evidence.quote: We train and evaluate a suite of OLMo-style models on the Dolma V1.7 dataset, using a standard Transformer++ implementation
Our experiments consist of a sweep of language model pretraining runs over $N\in[30,60,110,220]$ million parameters (non-embedding) and $D\in[1.5,3,6,13,26]$ billion tokens.
we train up to a very high $D/N\approx 10^{3}$ to study data scaling and set off over 20 runs at every $(N,D)$: we sweep 8 values of precision for each of the (weights, activations, attention).
We sweep the training precisions of the weights, activations, and KV cache $P_{\text{w}},P_{\text{a}},P_{\text{kv}}\in[3,12]$ individually, as well as training BF16 baselines.
We fit on over 465 pretraining runs and validate our predictions on model sizes up to 1.7B parameters trained on up to 26B tokens.

findings.text: 后训练量化带来的损失退化随训练数据量增加而增大，对于固定模型，当 D/N 足够大或 P_post 足够小时，量化后损失可能随预训练时间延长而增加 [S3.SS1.p1][S3.SS1.p3]。训练中量化权重、激活和 KV 缓存的效果可被建模为独立且乘性的，统一通过 N_eff 影响损失 [S4.SS2.p5]。当 N、D、P 联合优化时，计算最优预训练精度与计算预算无关，拟合结果约为 7-8 比特 [S4.SS3.SSS2.p1][S4.SS3.SSS3.p2]。当 N 固定时，计算最优精度随计算预算对数增长 [S4.SS3.SSS3.p1][S4.SS3.SSS3.p2]。统一缩放定律在超过 1000 个数据点上取得 R²=0.90 的拟合 [S5.p6]。

evidence.quote: We find that the degradation $\delta_{\text{PTQ}}$ increases in training data size across all model sizes, but that for a fixed dataset size larger models incur a smaller degradation.
This implies that when $D/N$ is sufficiently large, or $P_{\text{post}}$ sufficiently small, loss after quantization can increase as models are pretrained for longer
The effects of quantizing the weights, activations, and KV cache during training are well modeled as independent and multiplicative
which reveals that in general the optimal pretraining precision is independent of compute budget.
We find this $P^{*}$ to be around 7-8 bits when fitting our scaling law on runs with quantization done to integer type.
our scaling laws predict that models of differing sizes should not necessarily be trained in the same precision, and that compute-optimal precision scales as $P^{*}(C)\propto\log C$.
When $N,D,P$ are optimized jointly, compute-optimal pretraining precision is independent of compute.
In contrast, when $N$ is fixed in advance, such as when training a model family on similar data, $P^{*}(C)\propto\log C$.
we find a strong fit with $R^{2}=0.90$ on over 1000 data points (each of 465 pretraining runs post-train quantized to multiple precisions).

limitations.text: 作者承认，全文使用固定架构来考察精度、参数和 token 的影响，而低精度训练常涉及架构调整，可能缩小与全精度模型的差距 [S6.p2]。计算成本虽随精度线性缩放，但由于系统开销，减半精度带来的收益通常不到 2 倍 [S6.p2]。作者仅考虑损失缩放，未进行下游模型评估 [S6.p2]。作者强调所发现的趋势旨在提供启示而非规定性结论，并希望未来工作能在更大模型规模上更全面地检验这些效应 [S6.p2]。

evidence.quote: First, we use a fixed architecture throughout to examine the effects of precision, parameters, and tokens in a controlled manner.
In contrast, low precision training often involves architectural tweaks that can close much of the gap from a vanilla full precision model.
Second, while compute costs do scale linearly with precision, the gains from halving precision are usually less than 2x due to systems overhead.
Third, we only consider loss scaling without downstream model evaluations.
We emphasize that the trends we find aim to be suggestive rather than prescriptive, and hope future work can more comprehensively examine these effects at larger model scale.
